title: Publish from Cinema 4D (beta) | Verse Engine by Ctruh
description: Publish a scene from Cinema 4D to a shareable link with Verse Engine by Ctruh. Step-by-step guide to install, publish and share.

docs.article:
Publish from Cinema 4D#

**Status: 4.0.0-beta.1 — built and unit-tested, needs a real Cinema 4D install.** The plug-in's code ran against a fake c4d module: glTF vs. FBX, the exporter options, the document's units and bounding box, the units check, selection isolation, the dialog's timer-driven progress, the link on the clipboard, Cancel and the settings. A GLB it exported was published to a real local Verse server and finished (web/test/fix-verify-aec.mjs). VersePublish.pyp parses but has not been run inside Cinema 4D yet.

Three commands under Extensions ▸ Verse Publish: Publish to Verse, Publish selection to Verse and Verse settings…. The document is exported with Cinema 4D's own glTF exporter as GLB, uploaded with progress, and the share link is copied and opened — a link that opens on any phone.

You need: Cinema 4D 2023 or newer. Windows or macOS.

1. Install#

Download VersePublish-Cinema4D-4.0.0-beta.1.zip from the downloads page once the packages are published, or build it:

Code
sh integrations/aec/cinema4d/make_package.sh   # -> integrations/aec/cinema4d/dist/VersePublish-Cinema4D-4.0.0-beta.1.zip

Unzip and copy the VersePublish folder into Cinema 4D's plugins folder (Preferences ▸ Open Preferences Folder… ▸ plugins), or add the unzipped folder under Preferences ▸ Plugins ▸ Search Paths. Restart Cinema 4D.

2. Server and key#

Extensions ▸ Verse Publish ▸ Verse settings… — server URL (default https://verse.ctruh.com), API key, account token (from Studio), bake lighting, open the link when done, and Use … for every Verse plug-in.

Nothing is compiled in. Settings live in the per-user settings.json every Verse plug-in shares (%APPDATA%\Ctruh\VersePublish\settings.json on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Ctruh/VersePublish/settings.json on macOS), cinema4d section. VERSE_SERVER, VERSE_API_KEY, VERSE_TOKEN override it.

3. Publish#

  1. Publish to Verse — or select objects and **Publish selection to Verse** (they are copied into a temporary document; yours is untouched).
  2. A small dialog shows uploading % → building stages, and the status bar shows progress. Cinema 4D stays usable. Cancel (or closing the dialog) stops it and tells you whether anything was published.
  3. Published! — the link is on the clipboard and opens in the browser.

Success looks like: Published! with the link (also on the clipboard, and opened in the browser); a 100 cm cube measures 1 m in the viewer.

What gets exported#

  • GLB through Cinema 4D's glTF exporter (binary, current frame).
  • FBX with embedded textures if the glTF exporter is unavailable; the server converts it — Upload FBX and OBJ.
  • Units. Cinema 4D's default unit is the centimetre. The plug-in reads the document unit and measures the exported GLB against the document's bounding box; raw centimetre numbers are wrapped in one metre-scale root node (no vertex changed), metres are left alone. A 100 cm cube measures 1 m in the link.
  • Redshift / Octane materials are not glTF materials; bake or use standard materials with image textures for the best match.

Troubleshooting#

Every problem ends in one sentence; the first words tell you which row applies.

You seeWhat it meansDo this
"Could not reach the Verse server at …"Wrong server URL, no internet, or a firewall / proxy blocking the plug-in.Check Server URL in Extensions ▸ Verse Publish ▸ Verse settings… (default https://verse.ctruh.com) and open it in a browser.
"The Verse server at … did not recognise the account token …"The token is mistyped, was revoked, or belongs to another server. Nothing was uploaded.Copy the token again from Studio, or clear it to publish without an account.
"The server did not accept your API key or account token …"This server only takes uploads with an API key; the sentence ends with its reason.Enter the key from the server's operator in Extensions ▸ Verse Publish ▸ Verse settings….
"Upload limit reached: …"The hourly upload limit, or the API key's daily quota.Wait as the sentence says, or add an account token from Studio (a higher limit).
"The server is busy right now. …" / "The server is out of storage. …"The server's build queue or disk is full. Your file is fine.Publish again in a few minutes.
"The upload kept failing …"The connection dropped again and again.Publish again when the connection is steady; a large upload continues where it stopped.
"Verse cannot build … files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."STEP / IGES / native CAD files are not built by the server yet.Export GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that.
"Stopped waiting for the server. The scene is still being built …"You cancelled after the upload; the server keeps building.The scene appears in your Verse dashboard (with an account token) when it is ready.
No Verse Publish entries under ExtensionsThe VersePublish folder is not in Cinema 4D's plugins folder, or the Console shows a load error.Copy the folder (not its contents) into plugins, restart, and check Extensions ▸ Console.
"Cinema 4D could not export the document as glTF or FBX. …"Neither exporter ran.Check File ▸ Export works by hand, then publish again.

Anything else: send the whole sentence (and, for a build error, the scene name) to hello@ctruh.com.

What has been tested#

Export choice and options, units, bounding box through child matrices, selection isolation, empty document / selection sentences, the polled session, clipboard, Cancel, settings — against a fake c4dtested
A GLB exported through the plug-in published to a real local server, scene donetested
VersePublish.pyp parsestested
The glTF exporter's option names in your version, SaveDocument, the async dialog and timer, the command registration inside Cinema 4Dneeds a real install

The plug-in uses Maxon's development-only command IDs (1000001–1000003); a public release needs registered IDs.
